title: A Lifeline For a Vital Community Service
author: Aaron
body:
Recall the difficulties and inconveniences you’ve had to work through during the recent lockdown. Now imagine having to negotiate those challenges while living in one of the most remote parts of the Kimberley, where keeping a business running smoothly proves a challenge in the best of times.

The Imintji Community Store provides basic amenities, grocery items and fuel, among other necessary goods and services. Located on the legendary Gibb River Road, it is a key resource for travellers to the area, while being an essential part of the community; offering a source of employment, an outlet for local arts and crafts, and supplying necessities for locals. 

Having an intimate knowledge of the region, APT staff soon became aware that the store was in danger of closing. Reaching out to the APT Foundation, a much-needed contribution of $10,000 was subsequently made in support of this essential community hub.

‘The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 10 encourages us to support the marginalised and the disadvantaged’, the APT Foundation Manager Madeleine Curtain explained, ‘and so when we were told about the Imintji Community Store, we could not allow such a valuable community asset to perish.’

The Imintji (Ngarinyin) people invite guests to experience the spectacular King Leopold Ranges. Here, APT’s Bell Gorge Wilderness Lodge offers easy access to Bell, Windjana, Galvans and Barnett River Gorges, as well as Tunnel Creek. In fact, its location presents as the ideal base for exploring most of the key highlights of the western portion of the Kimberley.

APT has enjoyed an evolving  relationship with the Imintji community over the last 16 years, as a result of the brand’s Kimberley Wilderness Adventures, which operates in the area. Where possible, APT seeks to employ local staff, and also provides space at Bell Gorge Wilderness Lodge for local Imintji artists to display and sell their work.

The APT Foundation looks to ensure the survival and ongoing viability of the Imintji Community Store, as it continues to serve the local community and provide a welcome rest stop for visitors to the Kimberley.
